overview: The Panama City Beach City Council created its Community Redevelopment Agency on November 30, 2000. It then created the Front Beach Road CRA by resolution on June 21, 2001 and adopted the redevelopment plan in August 2001. The plan calls for rebuilding about 19.8 miles of road in phased 'segments': widening, medians, sidewalks, trolley lanes, stormwater work, lighting and undergrounded utilities along Front Beach Road, South Thomas Drive, South Arnold Road (SR 79) and connector roads. Bay County tax increment paid for it, growing from about $0.9M in FY2003 to about $21-22M a year by FY2024-25. The program was also backed by Series 2006 ($54.8M), Series 2015 refunding ($42.9M) and Series 2020 ($35.1M) revenue bonds, and the FY2024-25 budget books interest on Series 2024 bonds. A separate 93-acre Pier Park CRA passes its tax increment, and most of its business-tax receipts, to the Pier Park Community Development District under a 2001 agreement with The St. Joe Company. The Front Beach Road plan was extended from 2031 to 2049 in 2019, which led to years of dispute with Bay County over cost. That ended in a 2024 agreement capping annual CRA revenue at $30M.

districts.name: Front Beach Road CRA
districts.created: 2001-06-21 (Council resolution); Agency created 2000-11-30; plan adopted Aug 2001; plan extended to 2049 by Res. 19-140 (Sept 2019)
districts.boundary_description: Runs the whole length of the city's Gulf frontage, from the eastern to the western city limits. It reaches from the Gulf inland to roughly Middle Beach Road, about 1,500-2,000 linear feet. Some parcels extend to Panama City Beach Parkway (US 98) or the city's northern limits. The main roads are Front Beach Road, South Thomas Drive, South Arnold Road (SR 79), Hutchison Blvd, Powell Adams Rd, Hills Rd, Alf Coleman Rd, Richard Jackson Blvd and Nautilus St. The sources give no acreage. The base-year assessed value was $616,607,224, and it was $5,668,334,499 as of 1/1/2024.

districts.name: Pier Park CRA
districts.created: 2001 (Public Improvement Partnership Agreement with Pier Park CDD and The St. Joe Company; amended 2014)
districts.boundary_description: About 93 acres between Front Beach Road and US 98 (Panama City Beach Parkway) at Pier Park. The site holds roughly 900,000 sq ft of retail, dining and entertainment within a roughly 1.1 million sq ft open-air center. The base-year assessed value was $3,228,452, and it was $141,347,319 as of 1/1/2024.

controversies.summary: In September 2019 the City Council voted 3-2 to extend the Front Beach Road CRA plan from 2031 to 2049. Bay County had asked for a delay to negotiate first. News coverage projected about $800M in county-funded payments through 2049 if trends held, and a county commissioner warned the county might have to raise millage. Two council members opposed the extension.

In March 2020 the city and county approved an interlocal agreement (Res. 20-85). The CRA would rebate 20% of county tax increment above $15M a year, and new post-2020 borrowing counted toward fixed obligations only up to $80M. The agreement noted that the county's projected contribution, over $700M, far exceeded original estimates.

In 2023 Bay County raised its millage for the first time in about a decade. Some commissioners blamed the beach CRA, and the county said CRAs could absorb up to 20% of its tax revenue. The PCB mayor accused the commission of spreading misinformation. One commissioner said the county had paid $172M through 2023 and estimated about $586M in savings if projects finished 11 years early. Another commissioner called for ending the CRA.

In 2024 the city and county agreed to cap annual CRA revenue at $30M through 2049. Reports estimated the cap would save the county about $2.7B over 25 years, with the cap expected to bind around 2028-2029.
The city used eminent domain repeatedly for Segment 3, 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3 right-of-way. Examples include 17138/17140 Front Beach Rd and the 16726 FBR leasehold, after voluntary purchase talks failed.

Businesses complained about long construction disruptions on Segment 2 (2016-2019) and Segment 3 (2021-2026). Segment 3 ran about 375 days late because of utility conflicts and a storm-drain redesign. One restaurant owner described parking problems and a lawsuit with the city, and said several businesses closed during construction.

The Segment 3 construction contract was awarded to GAC Contractors in 2021 and assigned to CWR Contracting (C.W. Roberts) in April 2022, shortly after work began. Project cost grew from an FY2019 estimate of $24.3M (including land) to roughly $31-32.5M.

In FY2015 the city rejected all Segment 2 bids because the low bid far exceeded the budget, and re-bid the project in 2016. In 2021 the Powell Adams Road Segment II bids also came in over the CRA budget.

data_gaps: Annual adopted CRA budget totals for FY2003-FY2016, FY2019-FY2021 and FY2026 were not found. They likely sit in budget resolutions (e.g., Res. 19-137, 22-211, 23-217) and city budget books on pcbfl.gov.

Actual revenues and expenditures are known only for some years: FY2020 revenue $13,085,513; FY2021 revenue $14,592,537 and expenditures $16,634,476; FY2022 $15,303,477 and $15,242,194; FY2023 $20,608,513 and $20,383,756; FY2024 $31,156,153 and $22,111,115; FY2025 $26,522,556 and $17,543,945. The schema has no field for these. Full statements are in the city ACFRs and the Exhibit A financial statements, which did not extract.

The original Segment 3 construction contract amount (Res. 21-127, March 25, 2021) and the amounts of CWR Change Orders 1-6 were not found. The DocumentCenter resolution PDFs are image scans with no text. The city's Segment 3 page gives only a low bid of about $28M.
The contractor and contract details for the South Thomas Dr / FBR Segment 1 construction (2009-2011) and the Richard Jackson Blvd contract (c. 2009) were not found.
Corradino Group, DRMP and PBS&J program-management fees are missing, along with Keystone, Morgenstern Phifer Messina, Rogers Valuation and Diskin contract amounts. They are in agenda backup packets.

Individual right-of-way purchase prices and condemnation awards are missing, apart from the $22,239.36 Palmetto and $31,882.50 PCBH settlements (e.g., Res. 22-200, 23-203 final payments for Segment 4.1, and the 4.2 and 4.3 parcels). They would be in resolutions and Bay County circuit court eminent-domain case files.

Official statements and annual disclosures for the Series 2006, 2015 and 2020 bonds, and whether the Series 2024 bonds were issued (FY2024-25 budgets book 2024-bond interest), were not checked on EMMA (emma.msrb.org). Underwriters and interest rates are therefore unknown.
The construction award for Segments 4.1-4.3 is still pending. Design-build proposals for Segment 4.1 were due Oct 22, 2026, so no contractor or amount is available yet.
Total Bay County rebates paid under the 2020 interlocal agreement, and the text of the 2024 $30M cap agreement, were not found. Bay County BOCC minutes would have them.

No CRA spending was found for City Pier/Aaron Bessant Park, beach access parks or trolley operations. Those appear to be city or other funds. In 2011 the CRA sought $9M in NRDA funds for a Long Beach Access Park; whether it was funded is unknown.

No district acreage was found for the Front Beach Road CRA, and no GIS boundary file was found. The polygon here is a hand-drawn approximation of the Gulf-to-Middle Beach Rd corridor. Bay County GIS or the CRA plan maps would have the real boundary.
Pier Park CDD bond amounts and debt schedules were not found. Pier Park CDD audits filed with the Florida Auditor General would have them.
